title: repair unusual ColumnArgumentRole used in case(), this is only meant for ORM cases

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

body:
### Describe the bug

A `TypeDecorator` class that is working correctly with sqlalchemy 1.3.x is crashing with sqlalchemy 1.4.x with a `sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: Column expression expected, got <sqlalchemy.sql.elements.TextClause object at 0x10702aad0>` exception.


### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy import Column, String, Integer, case, func, text, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import ENUM
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from sqlalchemy.types import TypeDecorator

WIDGET_CASES = ['lower', 'upper']

Base = declarative_base()

class DecoratedName(TypeDecorator):
    impl = String

    def column_expression(self, colexpr):
        return case(
            [
                (text(":case = 'upper'"), func.upper(colexpr))
            ],
            else_=func.lower(colexpr)
        )


class Widget(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'widgets'

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(DecoratedName(255), nullable=False)
    case = Column(ENUM(*WIDGET_CASES))


db_string = "postgresql:///sqlalchemy-bug"
engine = create_engine(db_string, connect_args={'connect_timeout': 10}, echo=False)
session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)()

# Insert a widget into the database
widget_id = 1
widget = Widget(id=widget_id, name='widget 1', case='lower')
session.query(Widget).filter_by(id=widget_id).delete()
session.add(widget)
session.flush()
session.commit()

# Extract the widget from the database.
# This code works with sqlalchemy 1.3, crashes with sqlalchemy 1.4.
widget_out = session.\
    query(Widget).\
    params(case='upper').\
    filter_by(id=widget_id).\
    one()

print(f'Widget name = {widget_out.name}')
```

### Versions

- OS: macOS 11.6
- Python: 3.7.4
- SQLAlchemy: 1.4.26
- Database: PostgreSQL 10.2.5
- DBAPI: psycopg2


### Additional context

The attached zip file contains a small sample python app that demonstrates the issue:

[sqlalchemy-bug.zip](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/files/7469305/sqlalchemy-bug.zip)

The README.md in the zip file explains how to set up and run the sample app to demonstrate the issue. The README also describes different bash scripts you can use to run the same version of PostgreSQL that we are using (via Docker) and for creating a database for the sample app to use.

If you edit `pyproject.toml` and change `sqlalchemy = "1.3.24"` then the app should run successfully. If sqlalchemy = "1.4.26" then the app should crash as described above. Make sure to run `poetry update` after editing `pyproject.toml`.
